target.definition: Cumulative areal mass gain in g/mm^2 as printed by the source paper; not time-normalized. The printed unit and sign convention are unresolved (see docs/SOURCE_AUDIT.md).

validation.observation_independence_note: Exposure-time rows within a Material/Current cell are exact multiples of the 5 h value, so they are not independent observations.
validation.leakage_control: Every row at the held-out current is excluded from that fold's fit; no interpolated or derived rows are present.
validation.target_unit: g/mm^2; cumulative mass gain per exposed area, not time-normalized

known_limitations: The production model is a linear rate model adopted in v0.3.0: it predicts mass gain per hour from substrate and current, then scales by exposure time. The benchmark recorded a 69% reduction in leave-one-current-out MAE versus the previous random forest.
Eighteen reported rows, but eleven of twelve non-base rows equal an exact multiple of the 5 h value, so the effective number of independent measurements is six.
The sampled exposure times do not add independent information about oxidation kinetics beyond the near-linear time trend assumed by the paper's table.
The printed g/mm^2 unit implies an implausible specimen mass change; the paper's intended scale is unresolved.
Current, travel speed, and heat input vary together and are not separable.
Validation leaves out an entire welding current; the linear rate model extrapolates in current, which is a structural assumption, not an observed result.
See docs/MODEL_CARD.md and docs/SOURCE_AUDIT.md for the full limitations.
